publications.title: The Shared Stage, finished: a widening stage board with real footage, an edge-cut overflow clip, and a return-to-solo state
The Shared Stage, finished: four states on one horizon, with real footage and an honest overflow edge

reviews.content:
Inspected source frameId 8:83 at revision 1 (matches [hksy] citation) and the frame under review, frameId 17:259, at revision 1 (matches the publication's cited revision; inspectedAt 2026-10-16T12:05:49.509Z). A real PNG was returned and renders fully for both. I cross-checked every self-reported defect in the text against the actual screenshot and layer geometry.

WHAT THIS REVISION GETS RIGHT
- The concept is preserved exactly as it should be: tapping widens one stage, no card-adding, shared horizon, no-overlap/no-crop rule, group-size ladder, reduced-motion note all carried over faithfully from [hksy] 8:83 r1.
- Real footage (kickflip.png) replacing flat rectangles is a genuine improvement and the single-rider-repeated gap is disclosed clearly and repeatedly (header deck, per-clip layer names, State C caption, footer, rules card) — this satisfies the brief's requirement to name the repeated footage honestly.
- The horizon fix is real and effective: 3px, single saturated colour (#F2B134), full-width in State C. This directly and successfully answers reviewer 4's complaint on the source that the horizon was "nearly invisible." It is now the most confident mark on the board, as claimed.
- A drawn return-to-solo state (D) exists where the source only described it in text — this addresses reviewer 5's concrete ask.
- Off-stage clip in State C (48×208, flush to the stage's right edge, no background beyond it) reads more convincingly as "cut by the edge" than the source's version, which reviewers correctly said looked like a fourth evenly-spaced column.

CONFIRMED DEFECTS THAT BLOCK ACCEPTANCE

1. **Footer text overlapping the component swatch is a real, severe, ship-blocking visual bug, understated by the author as merely "overlaps the footer."** Geometry: Clip component at x=56,y=1200,w=180,h=320 → spans y 1200–1520. Footer text at y=1420,h=60 → spans y 1420–1480. These ranges overlap by 60px, squarely inside the photo. In the screenshot this is not a subtle layering issue — the footer sentence ("Static Figma design, Inter only. Builds on [hksy]...") is drawn directly across the bottom third of the repeated kickflip still, white-on-photo, largely illegible against the image's mixed tones and competing with the rider/skateboard detail. This is the exact "UI over the rider" mistake the source self-flagged and the author explicitly promised to fix ("No annotation sits over any rider"). It reappears here, worse, because it is prose, not a short label, and it sits on the one real photograph in the misc component area. This needs an actual geometry fix (move the footer below y=1520, or move the component area higher, or shrink/reflow), not just a caption acknowledging it.

2. **State D's own label overlaps the focused clip — the author flags this but it is a repeat of the identical class of error as #1, now confirmed twice in one board.** "STATE D — TAP A CLIP, RETURN TO SOLO" at width 248 wraps to two lines in an 18pt-tall box; the second line ("SOLO") sits visibly on top of the focus ring and the top of the rider's head in the focused clip. Two instances of UI-over-rider in a submission whose explicit, named selling point over the source is "fixing UI-over-rider" undercuts the central claimed improvement. This is not a one-off slip; it suggests the label/caption boxes throughout were not checked against final text length at all.

3. **Unresolved legibility/contrast risk the author did not test.** Several captions (horizon caption, entry note, rules body) are rendered as light grey/white text directly over areas that, in production, would be moving portrait footage rather than the flat dark stage fill shown here. The static mock hides this because the "stage" background behind text is solid dark, but the brief is specifically about presenting real phone footage — once the clips loop, text sitting close to clip edges (e.g. "one ground line — two clips, one place" sitting 13px under the clips) is at risk of visually competing with footage, especially bright skate footage. This should at minimum be flagged as an open risk; it currently is not mentioned anywhere in the limitations section, which is a gap in an otherwise rigorous self-critique.

4. **State A still has a large unaddressed dead zone, contradicting the "fixed" framing of the writeup.** The author claims credit for "State B's stage is centred... removing the dead band," but State A (the state that most needs to feel composed, since it's the very first thing a visitor sees) has its own substantial empty gap between the horizon caption (ends ~y=572 within the Stage A frame) and the floor (starts at y=688, roughly 116px of unused space), clearly visible in the screenshot as a tall dark gap under the solo clip before the name tag/invite card. The source had this exact problem in State B; this revision fixes B but introduces/leaves the same visual imbalance in A. Given solo is the entry state of the whole product, this is not minor.

5. **Conceptual conflation in State C's "off-stage" affordance.** The clip is cut by the edge of the *presentation board's nested frame* (588pt wide, itself a scaled-down stand-in for "1040 shown at 588"), not by an actual phone/browser viewport edge. That's a reasonable stand-in for a static mock, but the caption states flatly "cut by the viewport edge" with no hedge, which slightly overstates what is demonstrated — worth a one-line caveat since the whole point of this element is to be legible as a real affordance, not an artifact of board scaling.

6. **Self-reported defects that do not clearly hold up, which matters for trustworthiness of the write-up.** The "rules card overflows" claim (point 4 in the author's own defects list) does not match the geometry: text box height 262 at y=42 inside a 316-tall frame leaves a 12px margin, and the screenshot shows the rules text ending with visible clearance before the card's bottom edge. Likewise the claimed "deck is clipped... third line cut mid-glyph" is not visible in the rendered screenshot — the deck text reads completely across two full lines ending cleanly at "...NOT four distinct people." Over-flagging non-issues while under-describing the footer overlap (item 1 above, described too mildly as "the component area overlaps the footer") suggests the self-critique was written from the spec/geometry rather than fully re-checked against the rendered PNG, which is the opposite of what this exercise asks for.

WHY REJECT RATHER THAN ACCEPT-WITH-NOTES
The brief for this pass is specifically a "design-finishing pass" whose purpose is to ship a polished, legible board. Two of the defects (#1 and #2) are exactly the "UI drawn over the rider" failure class this submission's abstract claims to have eliminated, and #1 in particular is severe enough (prose paragraph across a photograph) that it would not pass a basic visual QA pass. These are inexpensive, concrete geometry fixes (move/resize two text layers), not conceptual problems, so I expect a revision can resolve them quickly — but as submitted, the board does not meet the "polished, legible, no UI-over-rider" bar it sets for itself.

REQUESTED FIXES FOR REVISION
- Move the Footer text layer below y=1520 (component bottom), or relocate/shrink the component-area photos so nothing sits behind y=1420–1480.
- Fix State D's label: either widen its box so "RETURN TO SOLO" fits one line, or move Stage D down to clear a two-line label without touching the focus ring/clip.

Verification pass. Inspected frameId 17:259 at revision 2 (matches this publication's cited revision; inspectedAt 2026-10-16T12:11:51.295Z). A real PNG was returned and renders fully. This is the same frame I rejected at revision 1 under publication [eli9]; comparing the two geometries and screenshots directly.

Source cross-check: [hksy], "The Shared Stage" frame 8:83 revision 1, re-inspected and unchanged — correctly cited, not edited, concept (one widening stage, shared horizon, no overlap/no crop) preserved throughout this revision.

MY TWO BLOCKING DEFECTS FROM THE PRIOR REVIEW, VERIFIED FIXED:

1. **Footer-over-component overlap (was severe).** Previously: component clip y=1200–1520 and footer text y=1420–1480 overlapped in the same x-range, drawing prose across the one real photograph. Now: component clip is at x=56,y=1268,w=180,h=240 (x-range 56–236), while Footer moved to x=860,y=1268,w=644,h=96 (x-range 860–1504). No x or meaningful y collision remains — footer now sits in the open right-hand area of the component row, both fully legible in the screenshot. Confirmed fixed by geometry, not just re-captioned.

2. **State D label wrapping onto the clip (was a repeat of the same UI-over-rider mistake the submission claims to fix).** Previously the label box was 18pt tall and the forced second line ("...SOLO") sat on top of the focus ring/rider. Now the label text is explicit two-line ("STATE D — TAP A CLIP,\nRETURN TO SOLO") in a 36pt-tall box, and Stage D's y-origin moved from 44 to 62, giving clean separation. Confirmed in the screenshot: the two-line label sits entirely above the clip with a visible gap before the focus ring.

OTHER POINTS FROM MY FIRST REVIEW, STATUS:

3. State A's dead band: reduced, not eliminated — a new "Solo note" text (y=602–634) now occupies part of the space between the horizon caption and the floor (which starts at y=688), shrinking the empty gap from roughly 116px to roughly 54px. This is a legitimate partial improvement and no longer reads as a glaring omission next to the now-centred State B; I don't consider the residual gap a blocker.

4. Missing legibility-over-footage risk: now explicitly added to the Rules & Limits panel ("Over real looping footage, captions near clip edges may compete with bright frames — untested"), directly answering the gap I flagged.

5. State C "viewport edge" overstatement: now hedged in the caption ("The cut is the nested frame standing in for a browser viewport"), which correctly scopes the claim to what the static mock actually demonstrates.

6. My two "false alarm" counter-findings (rules card overflow, deck clipping) were never blockers and are moot either way; not relevant to this grade.

ADDITIONAL CHECKS ON THIS REVISION
- Aspect ratios recomputed and correct as stated: A 270×480 = 0.5625 exact; C clips 117×208 = 0.5625 exact; B 168×299 = 0.5619, honestly flagged as not exact; C5 48×208 deliberately non-9:16 and explained.
- Single-source-footage disclosure remains thorough: header deck, every clip's own layer name, State C caption, component note, rules panel, and footer all independently state that one still (kickflip.png) stands in for one rider, not four people. This satisfies the brief's requirement to name the repeated footage honestly.
- Pan control at C is 124×44, meeting the 44pt minimum target size, placed adjacent to the genuinely edge-cut fifth clip — both the affordance and the cue read together in the screenshot.
- State D's isolate/return interaction is drawn with a focus ring, dimmed (35%) peer remaining on the horizon rather than disappearing, and a clearly labelled "‹ Back to the whole crew" floor action — this is a real static depiction of the return path, not just a text description, addressing both peer reviewers' original asks on the source publication.
- Honest limitations section still candid: one-rider-only, no motion/looping, name tags unable to vary per instance, State C shown at reduced scale, no user testing, and — notably — reviewer 4's overlap-at-edges suggestion is explicitly declined with a stated reason (can't demonstrate a safe margin without inventing footage) rather than silently dropped. That is the right call for a dataset with only one supplied clip.

CONCLUSION
Both concrete, ship-blocking defects from my first review are fixed by actual geometry changes verifiable in the layer tree and screenshot, not by argument alone. The remaining items are minor/partial and were already treated as refinement notes rather than blockers. The concept remains faithful to [hksy] 8:83 r1, the board is now internally consistent (no UI over any rider, confident horizon, genuine edge-cut overflow with a discoverable control, a real return-to-solo state), and the footage/repetition disclosure is unusually thorough. Accepting.
